The lioness, identified as five-year-old Nosikitok, is collared with a GPS tracker by Kope Lion, a conservation NGO. While lionesses adopting cubs of their own species is known, this behavior across species is unheard of. Dr. Hunter emphasized that he knows of no other documented case of a large cat adopting or nursing a cub from a different species.

Accompanying him is 30-year-old Dutch goalkeeper Michel Vorm, who has committed to a four-year deal with the London club. Meanwhile, Gylfi Sigurdsson, the 24-year-old Icelandic midfielder, returns to Swansea on a four-year contract. Sigurdsson previously enjoyed a successful loan spell at the Liberty Stadium in 2011-12, scoring seven goals in 18 games while on loan from Hoffenheim. Despite reported interest from Liverpool and manager Brendan Rodgers, Davies stated that Tottenham's persistent pursuit and the opportunity to join the north London club were decisive factors in his decision. He expressed his initial reluctance to leave Swansea but acknowledged the significance of the opportunity.

According to Jiangsu's pricing regulator, Mercedes-Benz, the German luxury car manufacturer, coerced its dealers in the area to fix minimum prices for specific car models, leading to fines of 7.7 million yuan for some dealers. In response, Mercedes-Benz stated its acceptance of the decision and commitment to competition law compliance, asserting that it has taken measures to fully adhere to the law, as conveyed by a spokesperson to Reuters. The Chinese regulator's statement detailed that Mercedes-Benz and its Jiangsu dealers were found to have engaged in monopolistic practices by setting minimum sales prices for E-Class and S-Class models, as well as certain spare parts. Moreover, Xinhua reported last year that Mercedes-Benz was previously found guilty of manipulating after-sales service prices in China, which is the world's largest car market.

S4C, primarily funded by the license fee, faces scrutiny as the UK government initiates a significant BBC review. David Davies, MP for Monmouth, emphasized to BBC Wales that S4C is a "special case" due to its role in promoting the Welsh language. Despite this, ministers have suggested S4C should pursue similar cost reductions as the BBC. Labour has cautioned that BBC budget cuts could jeopardize S4C's funding, but Culture Secretary John Whittingdale assured MPs of the channel's commitment "within the next couple of years" and expressed his intention to engage in discussions with S4C's management soon. Davies reiterated to BBC Radio Cymru that the government recognizes S4C's importance, viewing it as crucial for the Welsh language's future. He also suggested that the Welsh Affairs Committee, which he leads, might investigate broadcasting, including S4C.

In August 1974, a body was discovered in Cockley Cley, near Swaffham, Norfolk. Norfolk Police have since conducted a second post-mortem examination using advanced methods. Det Ch Insp Andy Guy stated that DNA extracted from the remains could potentially connect the woman to a living relative. The initial post-mortem, carried out on the day of the body's discovery on a heath, estimated her age to be between 23 and 35. She was found wearing a pink 1969 Marks & Spencer nightdress and wrapped in a plastic sheet tied with ropes. Investigators are focusing on the possibility that she was "The Duchess," an escort from Great Yarmouth. Detectives believe The Duchess, thought to be from Denmark, was well-known in the area before her sudden disappearance. The latest examination

The study indicated that men in training favored women with heavier builds. Dr. Carlota Batres, the lead researcher, suggested this shift might be an adaptive response to ensure mating with women who are more likely to thrive and reproduce in challenging conditions. She stated that the results demonstrate the adaptability of mate preferences based on environmental factors, noting that the preference for heavier women persisted as long as the demanding environment remained. According to Dr. Batres, these changes in preference could be advantageous, as they broaden the possibilities of pairing with individuals better suited to withstand illness or food scarcity. Foreign Affairs Secretary Perfecto Yasay intends to bring up the South China Sea issue at the upcoming Asia-Europe Meeting Summit (Asem) in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, a major two-day event beginning Friday with Chinese Premier Li Keqiang in attendance. This summit marks the first significant multilateral diplomatic gathering since a UN tribunal's ruling on July 12, which invalidated China's territorial claims in the South China Sea. China has rejected the ruling, asserting the tribunal's lack of jurisdiction and affirming that its activities in the region will continue unaffected. The Asem summit, which gathers 53 leaders from Asia and Europe, including those from claimant countries like Vietnam and Malaysia, will also be the first such meeting for the new Philippine government.

After colliding with a car on the A9 while driving an articulated lorry, John McCormack continued driving for 30 miles. Perth Sheriff Court heard that the car contained three children during the incident. McCormack, 46, received a sentence of 250 hours of community service and a two-year driving ban. According to prosecutor Rebecca Kynaston, drivers traveling north near the House of Bruar shopping center witnessed McCormack's lorry heading directly toward them on the wrong side of the road. She explained that these drivers narrowly avoided a collision by veering onto the verge. However, the lorry proceeded and struck the side of a car carrying a couple and their three children, causing a scraping impact.

Kim Little of Seattle Reign won the BBC World Service award, topping a fan vote to become the second recipient. She surpassed Gaelle Enganamouit, Amandine Henry, Carli Lloyd, and Becky Sauerbrunn. The 25-year-old Little expressed surprise and humility upon winning, adding that women's football is thriving and hoped it would continue to grow. She accepted the award at her team's training facility on Tuesday. Mary Hockaday of BBC World Service English congratulated Little, highlighting her exceptional talent and the continuous success of women's football. She also noted the BBC World Service's role in recognizing female footballers. Little was Seattle's top performer.

Stafford Hospital was allegedly the site of inadequate care, with reports of patients drinking from flower vases and reception staff triaging emergency patients. Julie Bailey, founder of Cure the NHS after her mother's experience, received a CBE, while whistleblower nurse Helene Donnelly was awarded an OBE. Data indicated a higher-than-expected mortality rate at the hospital from 2005 to 2008. Patients reportedly experienced delays or complete lack of pain management, and food and beverages were sometimes placed beyond their reach. Donnelly, who worked in the A&E, voiced almost 100 concerns about patient care, ultimately becoming a key witness in the Stafford Hospital public inquiry. Following a "very difficult time," she expressed immense pride and honor upon receiving her OBE for her contributions to the NHS in an interview with the BBC.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) found that credit card companies had little motivation to help customers in persistent debt because these individuals generated profits. The FCA advocated for encouraging customers to increase their debt repayments whenever possible. This investigation involved analyzing five years' worth of data from 34 million cardholders and surveying 40,000 individuals regarding their credit card usage. The FCA observed robust competition for certain customers and products, while others were overlooked. Credit card providers promptly addressed missed payments due to their unprofitability but were less proactive with customers barely managing minimum payments. Joanna Elson, head of the Money Advice Trust, which operates National Debtline, concurred with the FCA's concern for the 1.6 million individuals struggling with minimum payments across multiple cards. She noted the report's finding that credit card firms typically intervene effectively when customers fall behind.

According to Alex Brazier, the Bank of England's financial stability director, outstanding car loans, credit card balance transfers, and personal loans have surged by 10% in the last year, while household incomes have only increased by 1.5%. Brazier cautioned that "household debt - like most things that are good in moderation - can be dangerous in excess." In a speech at the University of Liverpool's Institute for Risk and Uncertainty, Brazier stated that this rise in debt poses a danger to borrowers, lenders, and the broader economy. He also cautioned that High Street banks are susceptible to "a spiral of complacency" regarding rising consumer debt levels, noting that "lending standards can go from responsible to reckless very quickly." Brazier emphasized that lenders' perception of decreasing risks can paradoxically lead to increased risks for both themselves and the overall economy. He also suggested that the Bank of England

David Dallimore, an early years education researcher at Bangor University, is advocating for a significant reform of educational services for three- and four-year-old children in Wales. Speaking on BBC's Eye on Wales, he stated that a long-term strategy for early years services is lacking in Wales. The Welsh government has indicated that it will review its options after the specifics of the proposed Childcare Bill are available. Currently, all three- and four-year-olds are guaranteed at least 10 hours of education through the Foundation Phase. However, the implementation and funding of these hours for three-year-olds are determined individually by each of the 22 local councils, leading to substantial disparities in the quality and adaptability of services across different regions. This results in inconsistent provision, with variations in standards from one local authority to another.

Taking out the engines, unused for two years, would bring the number of operational vehicles in London to 142. The money saved would be used to hire more firefighters for Fire Rescue Units. However, the Fire Brigades Union (FBU) considers this permanent removal "dangerous and reckless." The London Fire Brigade (LFB) has presented three cost-saving plans, emphasizing that no fire stations will close and no firefighters will be laid off. The LFB claims it has maintained city-wide response time goals even with the 13 engines out of commission, adding that reinstating them would only improve first-engine arrival times by approximately four seconds. London Assembly Member Andrew Dismore has suggested a different plan.

Dee Stitt, a prominent UDA figure associated with Charter NI, faced backlash over comments he made to The Guardian. Charter NI's board expressed "deep disappointment and great concern" regarding the article, stating they would handle the issue internally. In the article, Stitt referred to the North Down Defenders loyalist band as "our homeland security" and claimed governmental neglect of Northern Ireland. Charter NI, a community organization, received a Â£1.7m grant from the Northern Ireland Executive's social investment fund. SDLP MLA Nichola Mallon asserted that Stitt's role within Charter NI was unsustainable and called for his immediate resignation, noting that Charter NI's statement confirmed Stitt's position as CEO and demanding his resignation.

Police Constable Frances Tilley confessed to ruining her career after failing to pay for a train trip from Bristol Temple Meads to Castle Cary in Somerset last June. During a disciplinary hearing at Northamptonshire Police headquarters, it was revealed she was still on probation, having served less than two years. Consequently, she was dismissed for gross misconduct. The hearing at Wootton Hall was told that Tilley journeyed from Northampton to Castle Cary on June 22nd of the previous year. The officer, who was characterized as "diligent, professional and committed," was traveling with companions and neglected to buy a ticket for the last part of her trip. Force solicitor Elizabeth Briggs stated that Tilley traveled from Bristol to Westbury and then to Castle Cary without a valid ticket for that final segment, despite having opportunities to purchase one. She added, "She said it was her..."

Reports indicate that a jewelry exhibition at the Carlton Hotel on the Croisette promenade, a prime location in Cannes, was robbed on Sunday morning. This incident marks the most significant in a string of notable robberies in the city, known for its annual film festival. Interestingly, the Carlton Hotel served as the filming location for Alfred Hitchcock's 1955 film, To Catch A Thief, which centered around a jewel thief in the French Riviera. At the time of the robbery, an exhibition of diamonds by the jeweler Leviev was taking place in the hotel lobby. According to local news outlets, the thief escaped with the jewels in a briefcase. The owner of the stolen jewels remains unidentified. Should the value of the stolen items be verified, it would rank as the second-largest jewelry heist in French history. Following Wednesday's 1-0 defeat, Spurs have now lost both of their European matches at Wembley Stadium this season, their temporary home for Champions League games while White Hart Lane undergoes redevelopment. Despite this, Pochettino insisted, "There is nowhere better in the world to play football. We were the problem, not Wembley." Spurs have the option of playing all home games at Wembley next season, including league, cup, and European fixtures. Pochettino expressed his embarrassment, stating, "After two games at Wembley, Monaco and Bayer Leverkusen, there is no excuse. We were poor and we need to find the answer in ourselves. We are very disappointed and we cannot show the performance that we have in recent weeks - that is the problem." The loss to Leverkusen came after a 2-1 defeat to Monaco in their first Champions League match at Wembley.

During a BBC debate at the University of Lincoln concerning the upcoming EU referendum, one panelist described himself as a neutral party under siege from "half-truths, lies and scaremongering" from both sides of the argument. The debate, scheduled to air on Sunday, also featured UKIP MEP Jane Collins (for Leave), Labour MP Melanie Onn (for Remain), and journalist Robin Limb. A key discussion point was the NHS's relationship with the EU. Ms. Collins, representing Yorkshire and Humber, asserted that the UK's annual contribution of £675 million to EU health schemes, with only £49 million recouped, was "an atrocity," arguing that leaving the EU was essential to revitalizing the NHS. Ranjit Singh Power, a hotel owner from Wolverhampton, vanished during a business trip to Punjab the previous year. While a taxi driver has admitted to killing him, the BBC's India Correspondent, Sanjoy Majumder, reports that local police suspect he had accomplices. Power's family is desperate to uncover the full story, expressing frustration with the lack of information from both the Foreign Office and Indian authorities. Ranjit's brother, Amrik Singh Power, stated, "I keep asking them questions, but I don't seem to be getting any answers... even today I'm pleading.. asking for information from the Foreign Office," highlighting their struggle. Mr. Power was last seen on May 8th at an airport in Amritsar, Punjab, and was reported missing after a week of no contact with his family. The taxi driver, Sukhdev Singh, who

In July, the University of Birmingham announced the finding of a Quran manuscript at least 1,370 years old, hailed as "a global treasure" by the university's Susan Worrall. The manuscript, which had been unnoticed in the university library for nearly a century, is available for free public viewing at the Edgbaston campus until October 25. A visitor expressed awe at the possibility of the Prophet Muhammad or his closest followers having handled the manuscript. Ms. Worrall, the director of special collections, conveyed her excitement about the discovery of one of the world's oldest Quran fragments. Muslim leaders in Birmingham, including Muhammad Afzal, chairman of Birmingham Central Mosque, have voiced their joy over the find.

Following Alastair Cook's resignation after a four-year tenure, Yorkshire's Joe Root has been appointed as the new Test captain. Root's first match as captain will be against South Africa at Lord's, commencing on July 7. The 26-year-old steps up from vice-captain, with Durham all-rounder Ben Stokes, 25, assuming the role of his deputy. Stokes emphasized the need to win while also captivating audiences, stating that they "want to perform in a manner that makes people want to come and watch us," and that "Test cricket is the pinnacle and we need people to fall in love with it again." Stokes affirmed that becoming vice-captain will not alter his approach to the game, emphasizing his desire to contribute in all facets, from scoring the winning runs to taking the final wicket.

Addressing soldiers stationed at Siachen, the world's highest battlefield claimed by both India and Pakistan, Prime Minister Modi stated that their vigilance ensures India's peace. Subsequently, he visited the flood-ravaged Kashmir valley, where at least 281 lives were lost and Srinagar was submerged, displacing over a million people. Modi is the second Indian Prime Minister to visit Siachen, following Manmohan Singh's visit in 2005. Since India gained control in 1984, more soldiers have perished due to the glacier's extreme weather conditions than in combat. Troops are stationed at altitudes reaching 22,000 ft (6,700m). During his Diwali visit, Modi met with senior officials and aid workers to assess relief efforts. The September floods in Indian-administered Kashmir damaged approximately 180,000 homes, leaving many still residing in relief camps.

The renowned Elephant and Castle nightclub in south-east London has been actively opposing the construction of an apartment building nearby, fearing that noise complaints from future residents might lead to its shutdown. While Southwark Council initially denied planning approval, Boris Johnson intervened and overturned the decision. The Liberal Democrat councillors who rejected the plan faced scrutiny when it was discovered that their party had received substantial donations from the club, which they failed to disclose during the meeting. Labour councillors and the developer, Oakmayne, were unaware of the extent of these donations until the BBC revealed them. Furthermore, the council's legal counsel had cautioned the councillors about potential legal violations for not declaring the contributions. Both Ministry of Sound and the Liberal Democrats maintain that their conduct was ethical and transparent. In a letter to

These changes would mark the first time Japanese troops could engage in combat overseas since World War II. Having already cleared the lower house, the legislation is anticipated to pass in the upper chamber. Japan's constitution currently forbids the use of force in resolving disputes, except for self-defense. However, a revised interpretation of the law will now permit "collective self-defense," enabling the use of force to protect allies under attack. Police are present on the streets, directing protesters to keep moving to reduce disruptions in the capital's core. Despite the rain, tens of thousands of demonstrators flooded the streets, urging the protection of their pacifist constitution and demanding the prime minister's resignation. Although police vans lined the streets, the unprecedented nature of such vocal opposition in Japan meant there was little concern about the situation escalating. These demonstrations, primarily led, have been ongoing throughout the summer.

On Sunday, she declared her intention to remain the MP for Brighton Pavilion, aiming to increase her focus on active politics. Elected in 2008 as the Green Party's first sole leader for England and Wales, following a change from a dual-speaker system, she also made history in 2010 by becoming their first Member of Parliament. Via Twitter, she stated her resignation as Leader was to allow a new leader to emerge. Elaborating on BBC Radio 4, she said her decision not to seek re-election was to provide opportunities for others to gain recognition and potentially secure elected positions. In her announcement, she highlighted the party's recent successes, including securing their first seat in Westminster, gaining control of their first local council, and their performance in the recent elections.

Corrie Mckeague, a 23-year-old airman stationed at RAF Honington, Suffolk, went missing after a night out in Bury St Edmunds on the morning of September 24. His mother, Nicola Urquhart, stated on the BBC's Victoria Derbyshire program that it was uncharacteristic for someone to simply vanish. She added that her son, originally from Dunfermline, Fife, might have willingly gotten into a stranger's car. CCTV footage last captured Mckeague alone in Bury St Edmunds at 3:20 AM BST, eating takeaway food. Tracking data indicated his mobile phone was in Bury St Edmunds early on September 24 before moving to the Barton Mills area. According to Ms. Urquhart, the phone data indicates the journey took 28 minutes, which is the typical driving time between the two locations. The whereabouts of the phone are currently unknown.

Regina Hungerford, a 56-year-old teacher at Merthyr Tydfil College, refuted allegations that she struck a 17-year-old student who was listening to music during her class. However, a disciplinary review determined that contact likely occurred, deeming her behavior "unacceptable." The Education Workforce Council suspended her on Thursday, stating that allowing her to return to teaching was in the public's best interest. Mrs. Hungerford admitted to yelling and slamming a book on the desk of the "provocative and disruptive" teenager as he listened to rap music, but she consistently denied hitting his head. Although she was acquitted on appeal of a criminal charge for assaulting the student during a math lesson for students with learning challenges, a disciplinary panel concluded in November that it was probable she made physical contact with the student's head or hand. The panel determined that her actions were "inappropriate."

Eric Morecambe bought the Jensen Interceptor in 1968 and garaged it at his residence until its sale to an auction house in 2014. Silverstone Auctions, the buyer, commissioned Jensen experts Cropredy Bridge to refurbish the engine, brakes, and body. Morecambe, who passed away in 1984, was the only owner of the vehicle, which was dispatched from Jensen's West Bromwich factory on September 23, 1968. Silverstone Auctions, based in Warwickshire and Hertfordshire, has detailed the car's history and restoration on a specific website. It features remarks from Morecambe's driver, Mike Fountain, who occasionally chauffeured the comedian and his wife, Joan, in the Jensen. Due to its design as a two-seater, space was limited, and Mr. Fountain recalled Morecambe often being "screwed up in the back". Despite this, the Lancashire native considered the Jensen his favorite car.

Following a Supreme Court decision, N. Srinivasan temporarily stepped down as head of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). Srinivasan, considered the most influential cricket administrator globally, owns a team in the lucrative Indian Premier League (IPL). Elected chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC) in February, he is scheduled to assume the position in July. Former Indian captain Sunil Gavaskar was appointed as interim BCCI head last month. The Supreme Court has directed the BCCI to form a panel to investigate corruption allegations against Srinivasan and twelve others, including some players, stating it could not ignore the severity of the accusations.

The procession was led by survivors of the suicide bombings at the Brussels airport and metro station, which claimed 32 lives. According to Belgian media, the march was a "calm and silent" demonstration. Originally scheduled for a week after the March 22nd attacks, the march was delayed at the request of authorities due to security concerns. Family members of the deceased, paramedics, airport employees, and people of various religious backgrounds participated in Sunday's march, carrying flowers to honor the victims. The route passed through the Molenbeek area, home to many of the suspected perpetrators of the Brussels and Paris attacks, and concluded at the temporary memorial outside the stock exchange. Hassan Bousetta, an organizer, stated to AFP that "When our fellow citizens, defenceless civilians, are cut down in a cowardly attack, all citizens should stand up to express their disgust and solidarity."

Uefa is considering adopting goal-line technology, but if approved, their current system of having extra assistant referees behind each goal would continue. The matter was debated by European football's governing body on Friday, with a final decision expected in January. Goal-line technology has already been implemented in the Premier League since the 2013-14 season and was used by Fifa at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. Uefa general secretary Gianni Infantino stated at a Paris news conference that there was a "positive" outlook on adopting the technology, despite some "logistical challenges." He further explained that if implemented for Euro 2016, it would also be used in the Champions League and Europa League the following season, supplementing the existing five assistant referees. While the ultimate decision rests with the January vote, the executive committee's current sentiment is quite favorable.

The company reported a net profit of 45.6 million Australian dollars ($32.4 million; £22.7 million), marking a 56.7% increase compared to the same period last year. Domino's attributed these strong results to "organic growth," asserting that it had overcome the challenges of the current global economic climate. The pizza chain also announced its second profit upgrade since December on Wednesday, causing its stock price to surge by over 10%. Domino's Australia, officially known as Domino's Pizza Enterprises and listed in Sydney, holds the master franchise rights for the Domino's brand in Australia, Belgium, France, Germany, Japan, and the Netherlands. The company noted that its Japanese operations expanded by 48 stores in the six months leading up to December, while its Australia and New Zealand operations are on course to open more than 50.

Carlos Brathwaite's four successive sixes against Ben Stokes in the final over led to a heartbreaking defeat for England against the West Indies. Despite this, Cook praised Stokes, calling him an "outstanding talent and an outstanding cricketer" with the resilience to bounce back and perform exceptionally in the future. Cook acknowledged the brilliance of Brathwaite's hitting, suggesting Stokes might want a second chance at his first delivery, although the second was nearly perfect but still resulted in a massive six. While admitting his devastation, Cook recognized the tournament's overall success, lamenting only the unfortunate final over. Meanwhile, Cook's county team, Essex, is set to begin a new chapter under coach Chris Silverwood.

Authorities suspect the man overdosed on heroin possibly laced with fentanyl or carfentanyl, both significantly stronger than typical street heroin. Police reported finding him unconscious at a residence in Fitzwilliam, near Wakefield, on Sunday; he later died in a hospital. A 43-year-old male has been apprehended regarding the incident. Det Ch Insp Stuart Spencer of West Yorkshire Police urged heroin users, especially those buying from street dealers, to exercise extreme caution about their drug source. This warning follows reports of "deadly batches" of heroin causing deaths in Hull, Barnsley, Leeds, and Normanton in West Yorkshire. In March, Cleveland Police connected six deaths in Stockton-on-Tees to a specific heroin batch.

Masai Graham clinched the "Joke of the Fringe" award with: "My dad suggested I register for a donor card, he's a man after my own heart." A panel of ten judges shortlisted jokes for a vote by 2,000 people. Previous winners of the Dave TV channel-sponsored competition include Tim Vine, Stewart Francis, and Zoe Lyon. Graham, from West Bromwich, secured the win after being shortlisted in 2014 and 2015, exclaiming, "It's an incredible honour to land Joke of the Fringe. Not bad for someone from West Brom!" Stuart Mitchell finished second with: "Why is it old people say 'there's no place like home', yet when you put them in one..." The judges reviewed an average of 60 comedy shows each.

Erika Murray, 31, was taken into custody on Thursday night following a neighbor's call to police expressing concerns about the welfare of other children residing in her house. Upon investigation, detectives discovered the remains of deceased infants within the residence, which they characterized as extremely dirty and infested with pests. Ms. Murray entered a plea of not guilty to all charges on Friday, which included concealing a fetal death, intimidating a witness, and allowing significant harm to come to a child. Her attorney suggested she may be suffering from mental illness. "People seek explanations in situations like these... but mental illness doesn't always offer clear explanations," stated Keith Halpern, Ms. Murray's lawyer, after her court appearance. Police initially responded to the Blackstone home after a neighbor was approached by one of the children living there, according to Worcester district attorney spokesman Tim Connolly. The ten-year-old boy reportedly asked the neighbor for advice on "How do you get a baby to stop crying?"

Jack Whitley, Chelsea's goalkeeper from 1907 to 1914, featured in their inaugural top-flight season. Upon his death, he requested burial in Brompton Cemetery, despite having moved away from London. The Chelsea Supporters' Trust has launched a crowdfunding campaign to fund a gravestone for Whitley, as it's thought his widow lacked the means to provide one. Official Chelsea historian Rick Glanvill emphasized the significance of a headstone for Whitley, stating it would "mean a huge amount." He added, "I'd been exploring connections between the club and the cemetery, as it's unique to have one next to a football ground. The 24-year-old all-rounder Stokes exited the game in Sharjah with his arm supported by a sling, the result of a diving effort to grab a catch. While fielding at backward square leg, Stokes dived, attempting to catch Sarfraz Ahmed off Samit Patel's bowling. England's Stuart Broad informed BBC Sport, "We knew immediately he was hurt when he landed." He added, "It's concerning, but we have sufficient batting and bowling depth to compensate if he's unable to continue." Stokes was visibly in pain as he lay prone, and after medical attention, he left the field, using his shirt as a makeshift sling.

In April 2014, Boko Haram abducted 276 girls, releasing 21 of them in October following Red Cross negotiations. While the released girls have remained in government care since then, they were brought back to Chibok for the Christmas holiday. However, according to BBC reports, family members stated that the girls were confined to a politician's residence, unable to return to their own homes or attend church services with their families. Instead, they were taken to a local assembly member's house for a reunion with their parents but were not permitted to go home. One distraught father lamented, "I can't believe my daughter is so close to home but can't actually come home," adding, "There's no reason to bring them to Chibok just to imprison them again. They couldn't even attend Christmas Day church services." Another parent recounted that a soldier seized his phone when he attempted to photograph his daughter, saying, "I took a picture of myself and my daughter, but the security personnel intervened."

Police identified Banjong Pongphon as a "key suspect" who held significant local power in their investigation. The UN refugee agency reported on Friday that the number of migrants from Myanmar and Bangladesh who embarked on smugglers' boats in the first three months of 2015, totaling 25,000, was roughly twice the number recorded during the same timeframe in 2014. Banjong Pongphon serves as mayor of Padang Besar, a sub-district in Songkhla province where 26 corpses were unearthed from mass graves the previous week. A report by the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) indicated that smugglers' camps located in the forests and plantations around Padang Besar are primary destinations for these migrants. The Wiltshire Police Federation, representing 1,000 county officers, has launched a public awareness campaign, including bus and newspaper advertisements, highlighting the potential demise of traditional policing methods. According to the federation, Wiltshire Police has experienced a reduction of 153 officers since 2010. While Chief Constable Mike Veale acknowledged the "impact" of these cuts, he affirmed the force's dedication to local policing. The federation's "Cuts Have Consequences" campaign asserts that Wiltshire has the fewest officers per capita in the UK. They caution that a 16% workforce reduction has led to insufficient response officers for emergencies, compromised nighttime community safety, and increased impunity for drunk drivers. The federation also reports that the force has already cut £17 million from its budget, with at least another £10 million in cuts anticipated. Federation chairman Mike White stated that staffing costs constitute 80% of the policing budget.

To honor Edgar Mobbs, a former England international and Northampton Saints captain, a charity match mirroring the England vs. Scotland game he organized on January 30, 1915, will be held on January 24, 2015, at Olney Rugby Club. Mobbs arranged the original match to enlist athletes for his World War One battalion. The commemorative event will feature players from the East Midlands against The 1st Battalion of the Yorkshire Regiment, with Olney Ladies playing the Army Women's XV. Mobbs, born in Northampton in 1882, began his career in Olney and captained Northampton Rugby Football Club from 1907. Capped seven times for England after debuting with a try against Australia in 1909, he rose from private to battalion commander, fighting in major battles and earning the Distinguished Service Order and two mentions in Despatches before his death on July 31, charging a German machine gun at Passchendale.

A new report from a charity highlights that over half of the world's 21 million refugees are being hosted by ten countries that collectively represent only 2.5% of the global GDP. Amnesty International's secretary general, Salil Shetty, urged richer countries to significantly increase their intake of refugees, citing the UK as a "sad example" of shirking responsibility. UN figures show the UK has accepted approximately 8,000 Syrian refugees since 2011, while the US has taken in only 12,000. Recent data from the UN refugee agency reveals that China, Russia, and the Gulf states have resettled no Syrian refugees. In contrast, Jordan, with a GDP just 1.2% the size of the UK's, is hosting nearly 655,000 Syrian refugees, and with a total of over 2.7 million refugees, it shelters more than any other country. Turkey has taken in over 2.5 million people, Pakistan 1.6 million, and Lebanon over 1.5 million.

On Monday afternoon, a CCTV camera recorded an incident outside Jonathan Gwyer's Whitstable residence, showing a man emptying the contents of his food waste bin into the adjacent general waste bin after inspecting it. Serco, the waste management company, has issued an apology for the "completely unacceptable" actions of one of its agency employees. Mr. Gwyer, a resident of Colombia Avenue, expressed his shock and disappointment, feeling his recycling efforts had been futile. He voiced his concern to the BBC, stating that such actions discourage people from recycling, making them question the purpose of separating waste. While Mr. Gwyer held Serco accountable, he did not want to blame the individual worker, acknowledging the difficulty of the job. He noted a recent increase in rushed and chaotic behavior among the workers. Serco released a statement emphasizing their appreciation for recycling efforts.

The Community Charge Debt bill sets a deadline to prevent local authorities from chasing unpaid poll tax. Voter registration increased following the independence referendum, and the expanded electoral rolls were used to locate those with outstanding debts. The Scottish government has pledged to compensate local authorities. The poll tax, also known as the community charge, was scrapped in 1993, just four years after its introduction in Scotland. This unpopular tax, which replaced the rates system, was implemented in Scotland by Margaret Thatcher's Conservative government in 1989, preceding its introduction elsewhere in the UK and triggering public protests. The total amount of uncollected poll tax has decreased in recent years, falling to under £350,000 in 2013-14, with some local authorities halting debt recovery entirely. Deputy First Minister John Swinney described the poll tax as a "hated levy" that caused hardship in Scottish communities and was widely regarded as an unworkable and universally opposed tax.

While both parties concurred on collaborating to combat extremism and stimulate economic growth, initial hopes for a comprehensive agreement diminished on Wednesday as each side released individual statements. Since the 2011 ousting of Muammar Gaddafi, Libya has been plagued by turmoil. Fayez Sarraj, the head of the UN-supported government, has been meeting with his rival Khalifa Haftar in the UAE this week. Haftar, who leads the eastern-based Libyan National Army (LNA), has resisted international attempts to resolve the Libyan conflict, refusing to recognize Sarraj's UN-backed Government of National Accord (GNA) since its formation in 2015. According to Reuters, a source close to the GNA leadership stated that the two parties initially tried to negotiate a joint statement on Wednesday before deciding to issue separate ones. Both statements emphasized the need to resolve Libya's political and economic challenges and for.

In July 2014, a Nottinghamshire woman from Eastwood repeatedly reported Craig Hutsby for making threats and violating his bail. The following month, Hutsby raped her. An IPCC report later determined that the rape could have been prevented if officers had promptly completed arrest forms. Detective Superintendent Rachel Walker stated that misconduct meetings were held with the officers involved. The Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) found that PC Sofi Essex should be held accountable for misconduct because she failed to create a timely "arrest package"—the necessary paperwork required before an arrest can be made—when requested. The IPCC stated that this delay prevented the location and arrest of Craig Hutsby before he committed the rape. The IPCC also concluded that PC Joseph Lovelock should be held accountable for misconduct for improperly filling out a form for the victim, which resulted in her not being identified as being at high risk of harm.

The victorious team claimed a $1 million (£650,000) prize, earned by defeating South Korean team Koo Tigers in the Berlin-held final, witnessed by a crowd of 15,000. SKT1 secured the championship with a 3-1 victory, with Koo Tigers being the only team throughout the entire competition to win a game against them. Gyeong-hwan Jang, an SKT1 player, commented in a post-match interview that they had a history of success against Koo, noting Koo's lack of adaptation over the past year. Gyeong-hwan Jang, also known as Marin, was recognized as SKT1's most valuable player for his crucial contribution to the team's second title win, despite only two players remaining from their 2013 victory.

Before his 2012 retirement, 32-year-old Taibu represented Zimbabwe in 28 Tests and 150 ODIs. Hightown's Nick Gordon, in charge of publicity, initially suspected a prank when Taibu contacted them. "After verifying his identity through Zimbabwean cricket contacts, discussions continued, making this a significant achievement for us," Gordon stated. The former Zimbabwe international, a wicketkeeper-batsman, is potentially set to debut for the Second Division team against Alder on April 24th. Gordon told BBC Radio Merseyside that Taibu reached out following the club's advertisement for an international player for the season. Gordon added, "Signing a player of Tatenda's caliber is a rare occurrence for a club like Hightown St Mary's. I was taken aback by the unexpected nature of it."

This meeting was the first of its kind since the normalization of relations between the two nations two decades prior. Despite their differing political ideologies, President Obama noted the deepening cooperation between the US and Vietnam. Experts suggest that the US and Vietnam are strengthening their relationship to counter China's growing assertiveness. This month marks the 40th anniversary of the Vietnam War's conclusion. Obama acknowledged the "difficult history" and "significant differences" in political systems, but highlighted the development of a "constructive relationship" built on "mutual respect" that has benefited both nations. Mr. Trong characterized the discussions as "cordial, constructive, positive and frank," emphasizing their transformation from "former enemies to become friends [and] comprehensive partners." He expressed confidence in the continued growth of their relationship and extended an invitation to Mr. Obama to visit Vietnam.

Following a video in which the Somalia-based group al-Shabab urged its followers to attack shopping centers in the US, Canada, and the UK, the speaker stated that he was taking the threat seriously. Al-Shabab was responsible for the 2013 Westgate mall attack in Nairobi, which resulted in 67 fatalities. Speaking to CNN, the speaker described the threat as representing "a new phase" of terrorism characterized by attacks carried out by "independent actors in their homelands." He emphasized the need to take any terrorist organization's call for attacks on specific locations seriously. However, he clarified that he was not advising people to avoid the malls mentioned by the militants. The video featured an individual with a British accent, his face fully concealed, calling on al-Shabab supporters to attack "American or..."

Following discussions with Irish Taoiseach Enda Kenny, the Prime Minister characterized the UK and Ireland as "close friends." Kenny expressed his satisfaction with the strengthening relationship. Cameron is scheduled to attend a state dinner with the Queen and Duke of Edinburgh, who are on a four-day visit marking the first trip by a reigning British monarch to the Republic of Ireland since its independence. Cameron stated that the visit highlights the potential for an even stronger relationship, emphasizing trade, investment, economic ties, and opportunities between the neighboring nations. He also acknowledged the Queen's "enormous sensitivity" towards the complex history between the UK and Ireland during her visit. While Cameron and Kenny previously met in Downing Street in April, this marks their first encounter on Irish soil since Kenny assumed office in March. Kenny had earlier informed the Irish parliament that he would.

These accounts, using names similar to official organizations like NASA and the Environmental Protection Agency, directly criticize President Trump, who has dismissed climate change as a hoax. The @RogueNASA account identifies itself as the "unofficial 'Resistance' team of NASA," clarifying that it's not an official NASA account or managed by government employees, but offering facts with a humorous tone. Similarly, @ActualEPAFacts, a rogue Environmental Protection Agency account, told BBC News their aim is to ensure the continued sharing of factual information about climate change and scientific research during the Trump administration. The account claimed to be run by three EPA employees who were motivated to act after being restricted from giving interviews about their research, following media reports that the Trump administration sought to limit communication with the public from certain government agencies, including the EPA. The official EPA Twitter account has been inactive since January 19, the day before Mr. Trump's inauguration.

The Labour Party is supporting the campaign to remain in the EU, and despite his past criticisms of the EU, Jeremy Corbyn is facing pressure to take a more prominent role. Members of Parliament have warned him that the referendum could be "lost" if Labour doesn't advocate for remaining with greater enthusiasm. A spokesperson for Corbyn stated that he plans to deliver a "big" speech on the EU "in due course." During a visit to Dagenham, Corbyn acknowledged that there are areas where the EU should be challenged, but emphasized that "at the moment we're campaigning because we want this sense of unity across Europe." He added that Labour's campaign focuses on "issues of social justice across Europe," including the social chapter, which outlines EU policies on workers' rights, and the Working Time Directive, which regulates employee working hours. Corbyn also mentioned holding meetings with socialist parties across Europe to garner support for his campaign.

At Preston Crown Court, Matthew Eteson, 42, from Hale, Greater Manchester, is contesting charges of gross negligence manslaughter in connection with the deaths of Kelly Webster, 36, and Lauren Thornton. The mother and daughter died in April 2013 while sleeping on a boat on Windermere. Prosecutor Graham Reeds QC stated that the family's Easter bank holiday trip to the Lake District to celebrate a birthday turned tragic when Eteson allegedly moved a generator from the deck on April 1st and used it to run a 1kW fan heater in the sleeping area. The court heard that disabled carbon monoxide detectors meant there was no warning of the deadly gas buildup. Both victims, from Leyland, Lancashire, were discovered deceased in their beds on the second-hand Bayliner 285 motor cruiser Arniston, with lethal carbon monoxide levels in their systems.

During scheduled maintenance on Reactor Three, EDF Energy discovered cracks in three graphite bricks. The company stated that the cracks posed no safety risks and did not affect the reactor's functionality. A comparable problem, referred to as "keyway root cracking," was discovered in Hunterston's other reactor the previous year. EDF Energy explained that it was disclosing the recent discoveries "as part of its dedication to openness and transparency." Station director Colin Weir emphasized that nuclear safety is the company's top priority, noting that they operate with significant safety margins, including those for graphite bricks. He added that the acceptable level of cracking is significantly lower than any level that would have an impact.

The London Array wind farm developers announced a three-year study to assess the potential impact of additional turbines on red-throated divers, a project intended to expand the wind farm between Kent and Essex to 341 turbines. This region serves as the winter habitat for approximately 6,500 red-throated divers, representing at least a third of the UK's total population. London Array has officially asked The Crown Estate to end the lease agreement for the phase two area and has also cancelled the reserved grid capacity at the National Grid substation in Graveney, Kent. The wind farm, located 10 miles north of Ramsgate, Kent, received approval in 2006, contingent on ensuring the protection of red-throated divers before proceeding with phase two, which would add 166 more turbines. Had Mr. McClarty rejoined the UUP, they would have secured two executive seats. His choice, however, leaves them with one, granting Alliance one by default. McClarty stated that hundreds of his constituents had encouraged him to stay independent, a commitment he intended to honor. He acknowledged his strong negotiating position, potentially allowing him to demand a ministry, but emphasized that his decision was not self-serving. He also expressed reservations about the UUP's organizational structure, describing it as a "loose amalgam of constituency associations" lacking "central control." BBC Northern Ireland's Gareth Gordon noted that McClarty, who left the Ulster Unionists in January after being deselected, refuted any suggestion of revenge as a motive. This decision will undoubtedly be a setback for his former party.

Robert Hannigan, the director of GCHQ since 2014, announced his resignation, citing family reasons. He expressed pride in his accomplishments but noted that two decades of public service had placed significant demands on his family. Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson acknowledged Hannigan's role in modernizing national security capabilities to combat terrorism during his tenure. Prior to leading GCHQ, Hannigan served as director general of defence and intelligence at the Foreign Office. In his resignation letter, he highlighted the life-saving impact of GCHQ's work both domestically and internationally, but felt it was time for a new leader to take the helm.

According to IHS, the "caliphate" that IS declared two years prior had diminished to 68,300 sq km (26,370 sq miles). This territorial reduction has prompted IS to escalate attacks against civilians in the Middle East and Europe, a trend projected to worsen. The previous week witnessed a devastating IS suicide bombing in Baghdad, claiming nearly 300 lives. This attack occurred shortly after the Iraqi government announced the recapture of Falluja, a city located just west of Baghdad. IHS reported that in January 2015, six months following IS's declaration of a caliphate, the group held approximately 90,800 sq km of territory in Iraq and Syria. By December of the same year, this area had decreased by 12,800 sq km to 78,000 sq km, representing a 14% decline. Since then, IS has lost an additional 9,700 sq km, leaving them in control of 68,300 sq km.

David Poole, 38, faced accusations at Cardiff Crown Court of providing false testimony in the trial of Adnan Khalid, 27, from Porth, Rhondda Cynon Taff, who was accused of grooming a 14-year-old. Poole, the founder of the "H Division" paedophile hunting group, had created a fictitious profile named "Chloe" on Plenty of Fish, posing as a 14-year-old, to ensnare Khalid. After communicating via Whatsapp, Poole arranged a meeting with Khalid in Cardiff and secretly filmed the encounter. Khalid, who maintained his innocence, claimed he believed he was communicating with a woman over 18. Judge Thomas Crowther QC ultimately delivered a formal not guilty verdict for Poole, after Poole admitted to falsely claiming he passed photo evidence to the police. The judge also criticized the actions of the paedophile hunting group, which led to the trial's collapse.

The 29-year-old Jamie Vardy rescheduled his wedding twice, first postponing it last year and then shifting it from June to participate in Euro 2016. England's coach, Roy Hodgson, acknowledged Vardy's need for a break to get married. Following his winning goal in England's 2-1 victory over Turkey on Sunday, Vardy confirmed Hodgson had granted him Wednesday off, but he would resume training afterward. Hodgson also noted Vardy's secure position in the team and the need to assess other players. Vardy, who scored 24 Premier League goals for Leicester's title win, began the Turkey match on the left of the front three before moving centrally to score the decisive goal after Harry Kane's opener.

NHS England has launched a walk-in service designed to decrease the need for doctor's appointments and curb the excessive use of antibiotics. This initiative aims to lower the number of GP visits, potentially saving the NHS millions annually. However, pharmacies caution that funding reductions in their sector could threaten the program's success. The Sore Throat Test and Treat service, previously tested in 35 Boots pharmacies, identifies whether an illness stems from a virus (rendering antibiotics ineffective) or a bacterial infection. A throat swab, measuring tongue sugars, yields results within five minutes. Patients who would benefit from antibiotics will receive prescriptions directly from the pharmacist, bypassing the need for a GP visit. NHS chief executive Simon Stevens announced the nationwide implementation of the scheme in the upcoming year, a move described as "quite an innovative step" by Dr. Adam Roberts, a microbiologist at University College London specializing in antibiotic resistance, in his statement to the BBC.

This action followed Russia's announcement of an agreement with "moderate" rebels to reduce conflict in Eastern Ghouta. However, analysts express uncertainty about the deal's enforceability. Eastern Ghouta was designated as one of four "de-escalation zones" in a May agreement between Russia, Iran, and Turkey. The Syrian army declared a cessation of hostilities in Eastern Ghouta starting at midday local time on Saturday (09:00 GMT), adding that it would respond appropriately to any violations. Faylaq al-Rahman, a rebel group, endorsed the pause and called on the government to honor it. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported isolated shelling incidents after the ceasefire began but noted the absence of significant combat. Prior to this, Russia announced the signing of an agreement with rebels in Cairo regarding the operational details of the safe zone.

In August, south of Brookmans Park, an A320 pilot reported a near miss with a white quadcopter drone that "flashed past" his aircraft. The UK Airprox Board's report stated that there was no time to react, emphasizing that a collision was narrowly avoided largely due to chance. Air traffic control confirmed that the A320 pilot, flying north of Potters Bar at approximately 18:45 BST on August 15, 2016, reported an object passing overhead. While air traffic control noted another aircraft had crossed above, the pilot described the object as red and white, with red and blue stripes on two rotor arms, and less than a meter in size. Regulations under the Air Navigation Order (ANO) 2016 mandate drone operators to adhere to specific articles.

On Tuesday, the hashtag #penuriecarburantdansunfilm, meaning "fuel shortage in a film," topped Twitter trends in France with over 5,000 tweets. This surge in online activity is linked to an ongoing strike affecting all eight of France's oil refineries due to new labor laws. Consequently, about 20% of the country's petrol stations are either out of fuel or experiencing supply shortages. French social media users are referencing films like Total Recall (a 1990 and 2012 sci-fi movie), a name also shared by a French oil and gas giant, Total. In a humorous vein, some users are also modifying film titles to reflect the situation, such as renaming Pulp Fiction to Pump Friction.

Following the discovery of cheating by 54 student officers, an investigation into the Garverville, east Belfast, college revealed a "pseudo-militaristic" environment with an excessive focus on punishment. The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) has agreed to 50 recommended reforms, and Chief Constable George Hamilton and other senior PSNI officials will meet with the Policing Board to discuss how to put these changes into action. Some adjustments to the 22-week training program were immediately made, including ending the practice of marching students to and from classes and the use of military-style "show parades" as a disciplinary measure. Student groups will now be called "classes" instead of "squads." The PSNI's plan outlines 34 changes targeted for completion by the end of March of the following year.

Their trip commenced with a visit to the Seamus Heaney Homeplace Centre in Bellaghy, where they had the opportunity to interact with the poet's relatives. Throughout their visit, the Royal couple will participate in various events in Londonderry, Belfast, and County Down. While in Bellaghy, they explored the visitors' centre, a place that served as inspiration for many of Seamus Heaney's iconic verses. Prince Charles, a long-time admirer of the Nobel laureate's work, had previously met him several times. Following their time in Bellaghy, they proceeded to the North West Cancer Centre at Altnagelvin Hospital in Londonderry to engage with staff and patients. On Tuesday evening, they were present at a musical event held at Hillsborough Castle in County Down.

The single-lane swing bridge spanning the River Weaver Navigation in Northwich, dating back to 1908, causes significant congestion. Local councillors supporting a petition refer to rush hour as "mayhem," and their campaign is supported by the local MP, Chancellor George Osborne. Cheshire West and Chester Council has announced an upcoming feasibility study to address the issue. The Winnington Turn Bridge, a Grade II listed structure and an early example of electrically powered swing bridges in Britain, forms part of the A533 connecting Northwich and the M56. While traffic can pass from both directions, the chairman of Barnton Parish Council, Dilys Hooper, reports typical waiting times of 40 minutes during peak hours in term time, describing the situation as "sheer mayhem" with drivers competing to cross first. With plans for at least 4,300 new homes in the Northwich area, Ms. Hooper expressed concern.

Posing as police officers, a group of eight men breached an airport fence on Monday evening and raided the cargo hold of a plane destined for Switzerland. They stole an estimated $50 million (Â£32 million; 37 million euros) worth of gems before fleeing through the same opening. Authorities discovered a burnt vehicle nearby shortly after the incident. According to a prosecutor's spokeswoman, the police are currently searching for the perpetrators. Caroline De Wolf from the Antwerp World Diamond Centre confirmed the $50 million estimate, emphasizing the enormity of the theft. Initial reports had suggested a higher value, with Belgian state media claiming 350 million euros ($468 million). An anonymous spokeswoman from the Antwerp centre described the robbery as "one of the biggest" ever, noting that the stolen diamonds were "rough stones" en route from Antwerp to Zurich. Antwerp is a global center for diamond trading, handling approximately $200 million in rough and polished diamonds every day.

In 2010, Cardiff had Wales' largest deficit at £494 million, equating to £1,450 per resident, while Merthyr Tydfil had the UK's highest per capita deficit at £2,268. Councils dismissed the report as "spurious," stating they had already addressed pension affordability. The Taxpayers Alliance analyzed 101 local government pension schemes across the UK, utilizing data from 2010-11 annual accounts and actuarial estimates to determine funding levels. The organization argued that final salary schemes were "inflexible and too expensive" and required immediate reform.

Data indicates that the postponement of the badger cull in 2012 incurred a cost of £2.5 million, followed by expenses of £9.8 million in 2013 and £4.5 million in 2014. Opponents of the cull have criticized the "disastrous" policy, arguing that it is placing an "unacceptable burden on the taxpayer." The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) stated that operational costs decreased by half between 2013 and 2014, with farmers covering additional expenses. Bovine TB, a disease transmissible from badgers to cattle, poses a significant threat to cattle farming. Regular testing of cattle is conducted, and those testing positive for TB are culled; in 2014, 26,413 infected cattle were slaughtered in England. However, concerns persist regarding the effectiveness of the culls in curbing TB transmission and the humaneness of the nighttime badger shooting. The figures, obtained through the Freedom of Information Act, were disclosed by The.

On May 22nd, 40-year-old Christopher Kelly fatally strangled 51-year-old Dorothy Beattie at her residence in Dunoon, Argyll and Bute. Glasgow's High Court was informed that the assault occurred following an alleged offensive comment made by Beattie regarding Kelly's children. Kelly, who confessed to a doctor leading to his apprehension, initially faced a murder charge but admitted to the reduced charge of culpable homicide. The court learned that Kelly had previously served as a support worker for Beattie, who had multiple health issues, including seizures. The divorced mother and Kelly developed a friendship and frequently spent time together. However, he attacked her at her home after she reportedly made "derogatory" statements concerning his children, grabbing and strangling her before leaving. On Thursday, State Prosecutor Marilyn Mosby revealed the updated charges in the Freddie Gray case, with the most severe charge of second-degree murder still standing. Gray's death, a week after sustaining a critical spinal injury while in police custody in April, triggered widespread demonstrations, followed by riots and looting in Baltimore. Mosby explained that revising charges during an active investigation is both permissible and necessary as new evidence emerges. While the grand jury chose not to indict on the false imprisonment charges Mosby had initially filed, arguing Gray's arrest was unlawful, they did return new reckless endangerment charges that were not included in the original announcement three weeks prior. Mosby has stated that Gray's neck was broken during the handcuffing and placement into the police van, and that officers disregarded his repeated requests for help.

Baboucarr Ceesay, a 21-year-old from Gambia, is presumed dead after the fishing vessel he was on capsized off the Libyan coast on Sunday. His aunt, Jessica Sey of Cheltenham, expressed her family's grief, stating they "will never get justice" and emphasized the need to better inform migrants about the dangers involved. She voiced outrage, demanding accountability for those who exploit migrants for profit by placing them on unsafe vessels. Mrs. Sey stressed that this issue is not isolated but directly affects communities like hers. She explained that her nephew's journey to the UK was driven by desperation for a better life. Although a talented football player with a comfortable life in Gambia, his desire for opportunity in Europe led him to take a perilous and ultimately fatal route. He and a friend initially traveled by boat from Banjul to Guinea, beginning their journey across the Sahara.

For two consecutive seasons, a machine learning algorithm has outperformed BBC football pundit Mark Lawrenson's predictions. Now, the team behind it is challenging fantasy football enthusiasts to try and surpass the algorithm's performance. Researchers suggest the algorithm could also assist players in creating more effective teams. Fantasy football involves users creating a virtual team of real footballers and earning points based on their actual game statistics. Invented in the UK in 1971 by Bernie Donnelly, the game has evolved from a small pastime into a thriving online industry, with users engaging through ad-supported platforms, downloadable apps, and even betting on game results. In the free Fantasy Premier League salary cap game, fantasy managers can compete against Squadguru's AI in the "Challenge the Squadguru" league.

According to one account, the explosion occurred while people were waiting in line for food. The camp provides refuge for individuals escaping turmoil in the tribal regions bordering Afghanistan, an area known to harbor numerous Taliban and al-Qaeda-affiliated militants. However, police indicate that the camp is also utilized as a sanctuary by some militants. No organization has claimed responsibility for the attack. Attacks on refugee camps in Pakistan are highly unusual, although there have been long-standing concerns about militants attempting to infiltrate Jalozai and other similar camps. The BBC's M Ilyas Khan in Islamabad notes that a government-supported tribal force detained individuals connected to Lashkar-e-Islam the previous week, and police suspect that Thursday's bombing might be a retaliatory act. Live television coverage displayed ambulances transporting blast victims to hospitals, and the police are currently examining the debris left by the bomb, which created a crater.

A city council report indicated that the July 2015 yacht races increased tourism and improved the city's image. The report also noted spectator confusion regarding tickets and disapproval of the steel fencing used at the venue. For the upcoming event, evening entertainment has been eliminated. The four-day event in July 2015, organized by TeamOrigin Events, served as the inaugural stage of the sailing series, where Sir Ben Ainslie Racing (BAR) commenced Britain's campaign for the 35th America's Cup. Although Saturday's events drew approximately 100,000 attendees, Sunday's races were called off, and public viewing areas were cleared due to inclement weather. The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge were among those who were let down by the cancellation, and spectator arrangements received criticism on social media.

To disperse predominantly Shia Muslim protesters demonstrating against corruption and inadequate security, authorities used tear gas and live ammunition. An imposed curfew in Baghdad has since been lifted. This marks the second instance this month of protesters breaching the city's government district. Shia cleric Moqtada Sadr denounced the forceful response and expressed backing for the demonstrators' "peaceful [and] spontaneous revolt." Reports indicate at least 50 protesters sustained injuries. The demonstrators fault the government for its failure to implement crucial reforms while grappling with the fight against the Islamic State group (IS) and diminishing oil income. The Sunni jihadist group maintains control over areas in western and northern Iraq and has claimed responsibility for numerous recent deadly attacks. Some protesters successfully entered the prime minister's office and parliament, both located within Baghdad's Green Zone, which also houses important government buildings and numerous foreign embassies.

In a public statement, Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister Peter O'Neill announced that he and Australia's Immigration Minister Peter Dutton convened in Port Moresby on Wednesday, reaching a consensus to shut down the Manus Island center. This decision follows the PNG Supreme Court's April ruling that the detention of asylum seekers and refugees at the facility was unconstitutional. O'Neill clarified that the Manus Regional Processing Centre, currently accommodating 854 men, will not be closed abruptly, adding that various options are being explored and put into action for the asylum seekers on Manus Island. He stressed the need for a deliberate and unhurried approach, considering the interests of Papua New Guinea's citizens and the welfare of the asylum seekers and refugees. It is worth noting that Australia diverts asylum seekers arriving by boat to offshore detention facilities.

BBC Three will provide weekly online coverage of the Gfinity Elite Series, where 160 gamers will battle for a £225,000 prize in front of live audiences. While e-sports already boasts a significant viewership, one analyst believes the BBC's involvement could draw in new fans. The agreement includes broadcasts of exclusive content from the Gfinity tournament in west London. The featured games include Street Fighter V, Counter Strike: Global Offensive, and Rocket League. Currently, Twitch and YouTube dominate the e-sports streaming landscape, though traditional TV channels like Ginx are also showing events. The BBC, having previously aired e-sports highlights, emphasizes that its Gfinity coverage will be "on a much larger scale." According to IHS analyst Piers Harding-Rolls.

This interactive display mirrors a phone's touchscreen, a complete computer keyboard, or piano keys. The laser projector also casts images and videos on walls. The Smart Cast phone debuted at Lenovo's Tech World conference in Beijing, alongside a new smartwatch. Lenovo stated the laser projector, measuring only 34mm x 26mm x 5mm, projects sharp images onto flat surfaces without needing focus. A demonstration video shows how rotating the lens mount transforms the device from a regular wall projector to "surface mode," projecting the display onto surfaces.

A survey conducted by the Metropolitan Police Federation aimed to assess opinions on firearms in light of the persistent terrorism threat. Out of 11,000 responding officers, a mere 6% felt the number of armed officers was "adequate." The Met Police has announced plans to add 600 more firearm officers. Since August 2014, the UK's international terrorism threat level has remained at severe, indicating a high likelihood of an attack. The poll revealed that 43% wanted more specialist firearm officers, while 26% thought all officers should be routinely armed. Conversely, 12% stated they would never carry a firearm. Key statistics include 2,139 authorized firearms officers (6.7% of total police ranks), 3,974 police firearms operations between March 2015 and March 2016, and 7 incidents where police firearms were discharged in 2015-16. The survey also showed strong support for Tasers, with 75% agreeing that all officers should have access to one. The question remains: Does the presence of armed police provide reassurance?

Geraint Thomas, 28, plays a vital role in Team Sky's efforts to support Chris Froome in his bid for a second consecutive Tour de France victory. Thomas expressed concerns about potential crashes, especially after Froome underwent an X-ray following a fall during stage four. "The cobblestone sections are inherently risky, and rain could easily lead to someone's race ending prematurely," Thomas stated. "It would be devastating for any rider to see their year-long preparation end in such a way. We're hoping for dry conditions and that everyone avoids trouble." Froome's crash occurred just five kilometers into the 163.5km stage four from Le Touquet-Paris-Place to Lille Metropole when he clipped wheels within the peloton. The 29-year-old sustained abrasions to his left hip and a wrist injury but quickly remounted his bike and rejoined the race after receiving treatment from the race doctor. Following Marcel Kittel's stage four win, Froome sits in seventh place overall, trailing race leader Vincenzo Nibali by two seconds.

This case involves a Virginia school district's attempt to bar a 17-year-old transgender student, born female, from using the boys' bathroom. The Supreme Court is slated to decide the matter by the end of June. With the court operating with only eight justices following Antonin Scalia's death, a 4-4 deadlock is possible. School districts across the country are grappling with the issue of transgender students' bathroom access, specifically whether to mandate bathroom use based on the sex recorded on their birth certificates. The Supreme Court agreed to hear an appeal from Gloucester County, Virginia, effectively suspending a lower court's ruling that had permitted transgender student Gavin Grimm to use the boys' restroom. Grimm, who identifies as male, publicly came out as transgender during his freshman year and subsequently filed a lawsuit against the school board.

Angus Campbell, leader of Comhairle nan Eilean Siar, highlighted the disparity in airfares, noting that the airline operating the Stornoway route offered cheaper flights to the Algarve. A Facebook campaign addressing this issue has garnered over 11,000 "likes." Loganair, the operator of the island routes for Flybe, has defended its pricing structure, stating that discounted travel is available for children, students, individuals visiting family in the hospital, and island residents. Campbell emphasized that reducing airfare costs is a key objective of Our Islands Our Future, an initiative aimed at securing greater autonomy for the Shetland, Orkney, and Western Isles councils. He cited an example where a round-trip flight from Stornoway to Glasgow on Flybe would cost £351, prompting islanders to question the high fares.

Following a Northern Echo front-page article in 2012, Cleveland Police is accused of attempting to track the communications of six individuals, including the newspaper's reporters, an employee, and a lawyer, according to the Echo. The police have not issued a statement to the BBC. The Police Federation has filed a complaint with the Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC). Reportedly, the force invoked the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act (RIPA), legislation regulating surveillance for crime-related matters or public safety concerns, to uncover the source of the leak. The Echo claims the application was filed after it published a story based on an internal report exposing institutionalized racism within the police force. A Cleveland Police spokesperson informed the paper that she could "neither confirm nor deny" whether a RIPA application was made to monitor the phone activity of three journalists, a serving police officer, a solicitor, and the chairman of the Cleveland Police Federation at the time.
