A study of employees and managers revealed that 25% of new fathers didn't utilize any paternity leave, while less than 10% exceeded the standard two-week allowance. The Institute of Leadership & Management (ILM) attributed this to deeply rooted employer biases and financial worries among new fathers. Despite government plans announced last year to allow shared parental leave, set to begin in April 2015, the ILM's findings suggest these changes will be ineffective without addressing employer attitudes. Charles Elvin, ILM's chief executive, stated that shared parental leave is vital for female advancement but that "cultural barriers" are hindering the use of both standard and extended paternity leave, with a prevailing "cultural expectation" that childcare is primarily the woman's responsibility.

On March 14, the Irish Coastguard Rescue Helicopter 116 crashed with four people on board. Following her rescue from the sea, Captain Dara Fitzpatrick passed away. The search is still underway for the remains of the other crew members. Due to unfavorable weather, diving operations were delayed until Friday. Garda Superintendent Tony Healy reported that divers were "actively working" on the seabed and would complete their current diving cycle, but would cease operations after dark. He stated that the primary objective remained the recovery of the crew. Jurgen Whyte, the chief inspector with the IAAIU, announced the successful retrieval of the data recorder from the seabed near Blackrock at 16:30. Whyte added that the recorder would be transported to Dublin before being sent to the UK's Air Accidents Investigation Branch for processing.

Since opening in October, the exhibition has attracted over 130,000 visitors. A key draw is "The Lacemaker," Vermeer's smallest known painting, on loan from The Louvre and making its UK debut. Due to high demand, the museum will extend its opening hours for the exhibition's final two weeks. "Vermeer's Women: Secrets and Silence" owes its popularity to the inclusion of "The Lacemaker," which curator Betsy Wiseman notes is rarely loaned by The Louvre due to its significance, comparable to the Mona Lisa. She adds that many people specifically visit the Louvre just to see this painting. The exhibition also features "A Lady At The Virginals With A Gentleman (The Music Lesson)" from The Royal Collection, and "A Young Woman Seated At A Virginal" from London's National Gallery.

In July 2016, the body of 51-year-old Helen Bailey was discovered in a cesspool at her Royston, Hertfordshire residence; she had been missing since April 11th. Her fiancé, Ian Stewart, is accused of her murder and pleads not guilty. Edward Farmer initially testified in St Albans Crown Court that he spotted Bailey in a car in Broadstairs, Kent, sometime between mid-April and June, but later conceded the sighting might have occurred several weeks earlier. The court was informed that Farmer claimed to have seen Bailey alone on Charlotte Street, near her vacation home in Broadstairs, "driving what looked to be a Range Rover or that type of 4x4, a dark colour," contradicting the defense's assertion that she had been abducted by two violent men and taken to the town. When asked about the date of the supposed sighting, Farmer estimated it was "about five, maybe six weeks prior to the police interview."

The Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes revealed anxieties among policymakers regarding stock market volatility and international economic fragility. Despite these concerns, they hesitated to express them publicly, fearing misinterpretation. The officials maintained a generally positive outlook on the US economy's strength, which underpinned their decision to conclude the quantitative easing (QE) program. This program involved the Fed purchasing bonds to maintain low long-term interest rates and stimulate economic activity. The minutes stated that members generally agreed there was enough fundamental strength to support continued progress toward maximum employment, justifying the end of QE. The US markets showed a limited response to the announcement, with the Dow Jones briefly increasing before declining again.

Robin Waistell argued that his inability to sell his Maesteg home stemmed from the rail authority's failure to address the persistent knotweed infestation on the embankment behind his property. This case was anticipated to set a precedent for homeowners affected by knotweed from railway embankments. Network Rail stated they would carefully examine the court's decision, and it's believed their request for an immediate appeal was denied. Following the loss of the Cardiff case brought by Mr. Waistell and a neighbor, Network Rail could face legal expenses reaching hundreds of thousands of pounds. Mr. Waistell, a 70-year-old widower, had relocated to the bungalow from Spain after his wife's passing, hoping to eventually move back but found the knotweed on Network Rail's land was preventing the sale of his property.

Rex Tillerson's remarks during his confirmation hearing, which are expected to escalate tensions with Beijing, addressed China's construction of artificial islands on reefs in contested waters. These islands, according to a think-tank, feature military installations as evidenced by images released late last year. Tillerson, in his testimony before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, compared China's actions to Russia's annexation of Crimea. He stated that the U.S. must send a "clear signal" to China to halt island-building and deny access to the constructed islands. China's island construction has sparked concern in the region, as Beijing asserts claims over almost the entire South China Sea, conflicting with claims from Vietnam, the Philippines, Taiwan, Malaysia, and Brunei. Despite an international tribunal ruling against China's claims in July, in a case brought by the Philippines, Beijing has refused to acknowledge the verdict.

The council disclosed that index-linked bonds might be issued soon, "subject to market conditions." Having already achieved the distinction of being the first Scottish council with a credit rating, confirmed as Aa2 by Moody's Investors Service, Aberdeen announced that the funding would back a £1 billion capital program. Council leader Jennifer Laing hailed the potential bond issue as a landmark event for the city. She emphasized that proceeding with the bond issue, after securing the credit rating, would mark another pioneering achievement for a Scottish local authority, highlighting their commitment to innovative public sector finance. Laing further stated that their proactive approach to capital funding demonstrates their dedication to safeguarding the revenue budget, which is essential for delivering services.

At the Chicago event, Gwen Jorgensen secured her second consecutive world title and 15th straight victory, leaving Stanford in second place and Holland in third. Jorgensen, representing the United States, pulled ahead during the run. Stanford, a former world champion from Wales, admitted to feeling the pressure of the selection criteria. Holland expressed her satisfaction with reaching the podium, particularly after breaking away with only two other runners. Jorgensen's total time for the 1.5km swim, 40km cycle, and 10km run was one hour, 55 minutes, and 36 seconds, with Stanford finishing 29 seconds behind and becoming the second Welsh woman to qualify for Rio, following Hannah Mills.

GMB Scotland asserts that the employment conditions of its offshore members are being threatened. Union officials will request authorization from the regional committee to conduct a strike ballot among members covered by the Offshore Contractors Agreement. This action mirrors a similar announcement made by Unite over the weekend. Several North Sea oil and gas companies have revealed plans to cut jobs and decrease wages in response to the continued decline in oil prices. GMB's decision comes after unsuccessful negotiations on Friday between the two unions and the Offshore Contractors Association (OCA), which represents offshore contractors. The Offshore Contractors Agreement encompasses workers in various fields, including mechanical, electrical, and related services, construction, maintenance, design, project engineering, fabrication, and decommissioning. GMB Scotland regional officer John Kelly stated that some oil companies and contractors are displaying "blatant opportunism" by attempting to drastically undermine the terms and conditions of their workforce.

Walsall appeared the more threatening side in the first half, but Albion's goalie, Jon McLaughlin, denied goals from Paul Downing and Romaine Sawyers. Burton's Stuart Beavon nearly scored after maneuvering into Walsall's penalty area, but his shot hit the side of the net. Following Wigan's victory over Bury, Albion's advantage at the top of the league has shrunk to two points, while Walsall remains in fourth place. Burton Albion's manager, Nigel Clough, commented to BBC Radio Derby that the game was tightly contested and unlikely to be a high-scoring affair. He acknowledged limited opportunities but emphasized the value of a clean sheet and another point. While he felt their ball movement was superior in the previous game, he highlighted the team's return to their established strengths of defensive solidity and denying opponents scoring chances.

During discussions with US President Barack Obama at the White House, the prime minister addressed the issue of extradition rules. These rules have been criticized for allegedly simplifying the extradition of UK citizens because US authorities are required to present less supporting evidence. However, a senior judge who examined the rules in 2011 concluded they were equitable for British citizens. According to the BBC's political editor, Nick Robinson, Mr. Cameron brought up the practical application of these extradition rules during the two-hour meeting on Wednesday. The prime minister is currently on a three-day official visit to the United States. The 2003 US-UK extradition treaty has faced scrutiny following contentious cases involving British citizens like Christopher Tappin and Gary McKinnon. Organizations such as Parliament's Joint Committee on Human Rights have called for the government to renegotiate the treaty, arguing that it is unfairly weighted.

Fiscal Kombat casts the player as Mr. Melenchon navigating city streets, battling oligarchs and political opponents to extract wealth for his policies. The objective is to amass funds while dodging potentially fatal attacks from wealthy adversaries. Melenchon confronts a series of "bosses," including ex-President Nicolas Sarkozy, IMF chief Christine Lagarde, tax-evader Jerome Cahuzac, and L'Oreal heiress Liliane Bettencourt. Rivals in the 2017 French election, Emmanuel Macron and Francois Fillon, also appear as opponents. Le Monde reports that the game originated from Melenchon supporters on the Jeuxvideo.com chatroom, and has since received the candidate's full endorsement.

A proposed merger between Bouygues Telecom and Vivendi's SFR would establish France's leading mobile service provider, reducing the market to just three major players. Altice, the parent company of Numericable, has also bid for SFR, though the offer's value remains undisclosed. Currently, Bouygues Telecom and SFR rank as the second and third largest mobile phone companies in France, respectively. Their union would surpass Orange, making them the country's largest. However, the deal requires approval from competition authorities in both France and the EU. The European Commission has already expressed competition concerns regarding a similar acquisition of E-Plus in Germany by Telefonica. Experts suggest the Bouygues offer aligns with a wider consolidation trend within the mobile industry.

Doreen Collyer, a 60-year-old former lecturer at the University of Chester, tragically died in a shark attack while scuba diving in Perth on Sunday. According to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC), a 16ft (5m) great white shark is believed to be responsible. Her husband, David Collyer, described her as a "beautiful person" and a "loving wife." The couple had relocated to Australia from Neston, Cheshire, approximately five years ago. Mrs. Collyer possessed an advanced open water diving certification. ABC reported that her diving companion was able to pull her out of the water, but she succumbed to her injuries at the site of the attack. Prof Annette McIntosh-Scott of the University of Chester, remembered Mrs. Collyer as a "hugely valued and loved member of staff" who dedicated 15 years to the Faculty of Health and Social Care, adding that she was passionate about teaching and child healthcare, always putting her students first.

Presumed to have been carried across the Atlantic by Hurricane Gert during its South American migration, the American warbler's sighting in England is considered a first, according to Martin Cade of Portland Bird Observatory, who described the event as "pretty amazing." These birds are common in the US, making annual migrations between North and South America. Cade speculates that the warbler may have been swept up in Caribbean storms and propelled to Europe with strong tailwinds. Another warbler has been observed recently at Mizen Head, on Ireland's southwestern coast. Cade noted that the robin-sized bird was "feeding well and appeared active," suggesting it may build up its reserves before migrating south towards Spain and Africa. Bird enthusiasts, or "twitchers," traveled from regions as distant as the Midlands, South Wales, and Yorkshire after news of the rare sighting circulated on Monday.

Arsène Wenger believes that Arsenal will not sell Alexis Sanchez, the 28-year-old Chilean whose goal secured their FA Cup semi-final victory over Manchester City, to any other Premier League team. Sanchez has one year remaining on his current contract, but Wenger anticipates he will extend his stay with the Gunners. While Wenger's own future at the club remains uncertain, with his contract expiring at the end of the season and a new two-year deal on the table, he affirmed that he is actively planning for the team's future, including identifying potential transfer targets. He emphasized the importance of these targets for the club's long-term prospects, stating he will continue working towards both present and future goals until the season's end.

Gene Palmer is the second prison employee taken into custody following the escape, joining Joyce Mitchell who has already been charged with assisting Richard Matt and David Sweat. These two convicted murderers used power tools to break out of the Clinton Correctional Facility, sparking an extensive search. Palmer was arraigned and released on bail, facing charges of promoting prison contraband, evidence tampering, and official misconduct. His attorney, Andrew Brockway, acknowledged that Palmer delivered the meat but claimed he was unaware it contained tools or that the inmates were planning an escape. Brockway stated that his client regrets delivering the meat and intends to plead not guilty. According to Clinton County District Attorney Andrew Wylie, Ms. Mitchell placed...

The H3 project, a joint effort to consolidate back-office functions across four Hampshire and Oxfordshire police, fire, and council organizations, aimed to achieve annual savings of up to £5 million. However, the Police Federation reported a "catalogue of errors" since its inception in 2014, including payroll inaccuracies. Despite these issues, Hampshire's Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) anticipates improvements by May, following further investment. A report submitted to PCC Michael Lane highlighted that H3 has created challenges in recruitment, staff sickness management, and has burdened police officers with administrative tasks that hinder their efficiency. Notable errors include incorrect pay for 1,300 officers in February 2016 and miscalculated allowances in March of the same year. Furthermore, in 2015, the BBC revealed that payment delays to Hampshire County Council suppliers had tripled under the new system, prompting criticism from Hampshire Police Federation chairman John Apter.

On Thursday, police arrested a 22-year-old from Sleaford and a 25-year-old from Bracknell, suspecting their involvement in multiple attempts to breach Microsoft's network between January and March. They face charges under the UK's Computer Misuse Act for unauthorised computer access. Authorities believe the two are part of a larger group planning the cyberattack on Microsoft, with the aim of stealing customer information. The South East Regional Organised Crime Unit (Serocu) executed the raids, seizing devices potentially linked to the crime, according to Detective Sergeant Rob Bryant.

Ariya Jutanugarn, 20, played a flawless round, carding six birdies without a single bogey, putting her within striking distance of the tournament record of 19-under. Mirim Lee of South Korea, the overnight leader, fell to second place after a 69. Catriona Matthew of Scotland is six strokes behind, in fourth position, heading into the final round. Jutanugarn is aiming to become the first Thai golfer to win a major championship if she can maintain her lead on Sunday. Having learned from her ANA Inspiration experience, where she bogeyed the last three holes, she exuded composure and consistency in her third round. Speaking to BBC Sport, Jutanugarn said, "I think I know how to play under pressure. I have to focus on what is under my control."

During an IMF meeting in Washington, Christine Lagarde stated that the UK's economic strategy "has worked." She minimized discrepancies between the IMF's deficit projections and the Office for Budget Responsibility's more positive estimates, attributing them to differing calculation methods. Lagarde, sharing a panel with George Osborne and Wolfgang Schaeuble, noted that deficit forecasts in election years tend to be conservative, assuming announced plans may not fully materialize. She also commended UK authorities for striking a balance between spending cuts and revenue generation, citing the UK's comparatively strong growth rates in Europe as evidence of success.

Transport for London (TfL) plans to launch a consultation on new regulations for private hire services, including requirements for an English language exam, a test of map-reading skills, a requirement for a fixed telephone line, and the ability for customers to book a week in advance. Uber has criticized these proposals, claiming they would fundamentally alter the Uber service that customers are familiar with. Black cab drivers, on the other hand, have been advocating for stricter regulations. Recent protests by cab drivers outside City Hall highlight the increasing pressure on city officials. Uber's app uses GPS to connect passengers with nearby drivers, providing fare estimates, and typically offers lower prices than traditional taxi companies, with drivers relying on technology for navigation. All transactions are cashless, using pre-registered bank details. TfL states the consultation aims to "raise standards across the industry," citing the rapid expansion of the private hire sector and advancements in technology. Uber, however, believes it is being unfairly targeted and that the proposed rules would lead to higher fares and increased traffic congestion.

Music festival "superfans," who are primarily male, shell out an average of £581 annually on these events, frequently choosing VIP access or enhanced camping. These dedicated fans are also more inclined to purchase music in physical (CD) or digital download formats. The findings are based on a survey of 504 UK residents who have attended at least one festival in the past year. Eventbrite, the ticketing platform that conducted the survey, highlights the significant role of these "superfans" in boosting the music festival industry, as they often suggest music and events to their social circles. Representing 28% of the festival attendee population, over half (54%) of these superfans are comfortable attending events solo. While they spend an average of £45 more per event compared to casual fans, their allegiance is not assured, with 46% expressing concerns about the increasing commercialization of festivals. The UK hosts over 100 music festivals each year, ranging from major events like Glastonbury and T In The Park to smaller gatherings.

Sterling gained significantly, increasing by 1.86% against the dollar to reach $1.32.40 and by 1.73% against the euro, trading at €1.19.57. The FTSE 100 initially reached new 11-month peaks but then retreated, closing almost unchanged at 6,680.69, a minor decrease of 2.17 points or 0.03%. In contrast, the FTSE 250, which is more focused on the UK market, increased by 68.75 points, or 0.4%, to 16,775.14. The property sector, which had experienced substantial losses following the Brexit vote, was buoyed by Galliford Try's announcement that it still anticipated full-year profits to meet expectations, causing its shares to jump 8.5%. Financial stocks, which also suffered after the referendum, performed better, with Aviva's shares rising by 4.26% and Lloyds Banking Group also seeing gains.

In April, a submarine caught the fishing nets of a boat 18 miles from the County Down coast and dragged it backwards, causing substantial damage. The skipper reported that his crew was fortunate to avoid injury, but repairs would amount to approximately £10,000. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has now confirmed the involvement of a British submarine, reversing its earlier policy of not commenting on submarine operations. The Royal Navy stated that "new information" revealed a UK submarine was responsible for the damage to the MV Karen. Minister for the Armed Forces Penny Mordaunt issued a written statement to the House of Commons, expressing deep regret for the incident, the delay in identifying and addressing the events, and their repercussions. She explained that the incident happened because the submarine failed to properly identify the Karen as a fishing vessel with nets deployed.

Kian Delos Santos was fatally shot by police who alleged his involvement in drug trafficking and resistance to arrest. However, CCTV footage seemingly depicts plainclothes officers forcibly taking the 17-year-old. Evidence indicates he was kneeling face down when killed. His funeral in Manila drew hundreds of mourners, some protesting President Duterte's violent anti-drug campaign, which has garnered support from those weary of drug-related offenses. Reuters reports that nuns, priests, and numerous children chanting "justice for Kian, justice for all" participated in the procession from a church to the cemetery. During the Mass, his father, Saldy, asserted his son's innocence and expressed outrage at the police, questioning their compassion with a voice filled with emotion. He suggested they should seek solace in churches.

The new 72km lane, built parallel to a section of the original canal in under a year, enables two-way traffic and caters to larger ships. During a trial, multiple international container ships successfully traversed the route on Saturday, under the watch of helicopters and naval ships providing security. The Sinai Peninsula, adjacent to the canal, is a stronghold for Islamic militants responsible for the deaths of hundreds since the 2013 ousting of President Mohammed Morsi. The Suez Canal, connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas, first opened nearly 150 years ago. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi believes this expansion of a major global shipping artery will stimulate commerce and create jobs nationwide. The canal presently manages 7% of the world's seaborne trade.

James Carragher, already convicted of sex offences in 1993 (seven years) and 2004 (14 years), is now on trial at Leeds Crown Court, accused of 50 counts of indecent assault allegedly committed between the 1970s and 1990s at St William's in Market Weighton, East Riding of Yorkshire. Two other former staff members of the now-closed Catholic-run home for boys with behavioural problems, operated by the De La Salle order, have also faced trial previously. Carragher, who headed St William's from 1976 to 1990, and the two other men are accused of abusing a total of 19 former students. Prosecutor Richard Wright QC stated that Carragher harbored a "committed sexual interest in children and young boys in particular," concealing his actions behind a facade of respectability.

After transferring from Vitoria Setubal for an undisclosed sum, the 23-year-old Cardoso inked a three-year deal. Speaking to Rangers TV, he stated his determination to adapt to the new culture and lifestyle, expressing confidence in his future success. He pledged to give his all to support both himself and his teammates in achieving victory, emphasizing the winning expectation at a club of Rangers' stature. Cardoso, previously a Portuguese Under-21 international, played in 23 games for Vitoria Setubal last season after his move from Benfica. He follows Bruno Alves, a full Portuguese international from Cagliari, as the second Portuguese centre-back to join Rangers this summer. Midfielder Dalcio has also arrived at Ibrox on loan from Benfica.

Morgan Tsvangirai, a well-known critic of Mugabe, and former Vice-President Joice Mujuru have announced their collaboration for the upcoming election, though the presidential nominee remains undecided. President Mugabe, who is 93 years old and has governed since Zimbabwe's independence from Britain in 1980, intends to run again. Tsvangirai told reporters that this alliance marks the initial steps toward forming a comprehensive coalition to challenge Zanu-PF leading up to the election. This alliance represents a crucial move toward unifying a fractured opposition and, if successful, would mark the first time since 1980 that President Mugabe has faced such a large, unified opposition.

During a meeting with MEPs on Wednesday, Jean-Claude Juncker affirmed his support for "democratic expressions" and pledged to respect Scotland's decision. In response to a question from Catalan MEP Josep Maria Terricabras regarding Catalonia and Scotland's potential EU membership, Juncker stated that simply requesting membership via a letter is insufficient. When Scottish UKIP MEP David Coburn later inquired about an independent Scotland's EU status, Juncker deferred, stating it was ultimately the UK's decision. He reiterated his respect for the outcome of the Scottish independence referendum scheduled for September but avoided pre-empting the debate.

A report revealed that prospective Harvard students posted offensive content in a Facebook chat forum, including jokes about child abuse, sexual assault, paedophilia, and the Holocaust, alongside racial slurs directed at minorities. This led to criticism from free speech advocates who deemed Harvard's response as excessively harsh. The Harvard Crimson, the university's student newspaper, covered the incident, explaining that the chat forum stemmed from an initial messaging group for incoming students. The subgroup, intended for sharing memes and more "adult" content, required applicants to create and post a "provocative" meme to gain membership. Upon discovery of the group, Harvard administrators initiated an investigation, questioning the students involved.

A notice of intent to gather signatures for a recall election against Judge Aaron Persky in Santa Clara County was submitted by community leaders on Monday. The move comes after criticism of Persky's June 2016 sentencing of Stanford swimmer Brock Turner, who received a six-month jail term for a January 2015 assault, despite facing a potential 14-year prison sentence. Turner was released after serving only three months. The recall petition notice asserts that Judge Persky shocked the world by sentencing Turner to a mere six months for sexually assaulting an unconscious woman. Michele Dauber, a Stanford law professor spearheading the recall effort with 50 other community leaders, stated at a press conference that Santa Clara County residents deserve a judge who prioritizes victim protection over the rights of rapists, emphasizing that women are fed up with rape culture and prepared to take action.

Participants in the yearly competition have five minutes to deliver the most outrageous and believable lie possible. This year's winner, George Kemp from Maryport, Cumbria, expressed surprise at his victory, citing a troublesome chest infection. His winning fabrication involved "bumping into Donald Trump and his wife in an underwater hotel." He elaborated, "It was a story about constructing a miniature submarine from my dad's old bubble car. We journeyed to the Isle of Man and encountered numerous celebrities in a Scottish submarine crafted from shortbread tins. Nicola Sturgeon and Alex Salmond then sold these oversized shortbread tin submarines to the United States." Last year's champion, Mike Naylor, also known as Monkey Liar, from Wasdale, secured second place, while Helen Jordan finished third. Past victors include comedian and TV personality Sue Perkins.

The investigation revealed that only 28% of Welsh speakers had communicated in Welsh with their primary healthcare providers (GPs, dentists, and opticians). Ms. Huws expressed hope that her report would mark the end of patients being unable to access healthcare tailored to their needs. Government ministers welcomed the report and pledged a response within six months. Based on the experiences of over a thousand Welsh speakers, the inquiry highlighted that 90% believed they should have the right to use Welsh when interacting with the NHS, regardless of their location in Wales. Additional findings included reports from Welsh speakers who felt uncomfortable and struggled to articulate their feelings to English-speaking doctors. The report proposes 33 recommendations to the Welsh government, urging ministers to provide clear policy guidance to primary care providers, alongside an action plan and a timeline for implementing changes.

The proposed legislation seeks to repeal portions of the UK government's 2016 Trade Union Act, potentially altering existing limitations on industrial action within the NHS, fire service, schools, and other devolved Welsh services. While UK ministers maintain that industrial relations fall under Westminster's jurisdiction, the UK law mandates that strikes require the support of 40% of a union's membership in a ballot to be authorized. However, members of the Welsh Assembly's Equality, Local Government and Communities Committee supported the new bill to preserve Wales' "social-partnership" model. Welsh Finance Secretary Mark Drakeford warned in March that it would be a "democratic outrage" if London attempted to obstruct the Welsh Trade Union Bill. The Labour Welsh Government contends that UK ministers should not impose restrictions on union activities in devolved sectors like the NHS and schools. The committee report received the support of seven of the eight members, with Conservative AM Janet Finch-Saunders dissenting.

Following the death of 11-year-old Evha Jannath, who fell from a boat on Drayton Manor's Splash Canyon ride during a school trip on Tuesday, several theme parks have taken action. Drayton Manor will remain closed on Friday as investigations into health and safety are conducted. Merlin Entertainments, which operates Alton Towers and Legoland Windsor, has temporarily closed similar water rides as a precaution after learning of the incident. The company anticipates reopening these rides on Friday. However, some parks, such as Lightwater Valley and West Midland Safari Park, have not closed their water rides in response to the Drayton Manor tragedy.

Ally Gilchrist's own goal and a powerful shot from James Tavernier gave the Championship champions a commanding lead. A penalty from Andy Halliday and a close-range finish from Kenny Miller sealed the victory for Rangers, securing the trophy after three previous failed attempts. Mark Warburton's team will now face Celtic in the Scottish Cup semi-final next Sunday. Rangers' triumph in the Challenge Cup comes after past defeats to Queen of the South, Raith Rovers, and Alloa Athletic in earlier versions of the tournament. Their focus now shifts to a match against Premiership leaders at the national stadium, which will have a new pitch installed by then due to the poor condition of the previous surface used by Rangers and League One's Peterhead. The £200,000 pitch, laid just five weeks prior, is being replaced due to its failure to settle. Peterhead entered the match as significant underdogs at 22-1.

For the first time in its 134-year history, the Royal College of Midwives (RCM) members have voted overwhelmingly, by a margin of 9 to 1, to engage in a four-hour work stoppage. In response, the Department of Health expressed its disappointment and pledged to collaborate with trusts to maintain safe care for mothers and infants, emphasizing its willingness to engage in dialogue. The RCM is urgently requesting discussions with the health minister to address the disagreement. According to RCM NI director Bredagh Hughes, midwives are demanding the same 1% pay raise that has been granted to their counterparts in Wales, Scotland, and England. Hughes clarified that the dispute is with the Department of Health and employers, not with the women they serve, assuring that emergency services will be fully staffed and no woman will be endangered, even if striking midwives are needed to fill in.

Tesco Bank stated that the actual number of current account customers impacted by the recent fraud is less than 10,000, a figure lower than the initially reported 20,000. The bank confirmed that personal data remained secure during the "systematic, sophisticated attack" over the weekend, and that all affected accounts have been fully reimbursed. CEO Benny Higgins announced the restoration of normal account access, including the lifting of the suspension on online debit transactions. The suspension, implemented on Sunday to thwart criminal activity, had prevented current account customers from making online debit card payments. Mr. Higgins reiterated the bank's apology for the concern and disruption caused, adding that they have a clear understanding of the attack's nature.

A BBC London/Newsnight investigation uncovered widespread cheating in the Construction Skills Certification Scheme (CSCS), which requires construction workers to hold a card demonstrating their skills and health and safety knowledge. According to Carl Rhymer of the Construction Industry Training Board (CITB), a test provider, 6,000 cardholders will need to retake the exam. The CSCS card is considered the UK's premier certification for builders and is mandatory for nine of the UK's largest construction firms, as well as projects like Crossrail and Heathrow. The investigation revealed that several test centers were offering guaranteed passes for a fee, allowing workers with limited English skills to gain qualifications and access hazardous construction sites. Wep HSE in Ealing was exposed after its director, Garet Estensen, read out exam answers from a screen, instructing candidates to follow his lead. Mr. Estensen declined to comment when confronted with the evidence. Future Training 4 was another center exposed during the investigation.

The cyber attackers are demanding a ransom of 100 Bitcoin, equivalent to approximately $70,000 (£56,000 ; €66,000). In response, staff preemptively deactivated all ticketing machines connected to the network. Computers throughout the city's transportation system, including those at stations, were rendered inoperable and displayed a message from the hackers stating: "You Hacked, ALL Data Encrypted. Contact For Key(cryptom27@yandex.com)ID:681 ,Enter”. Yandex, a Russian internet corporation, offers services such as email and social networking. While the trains themselves remained unaffected, city authorities have launched a comprehensive investigation. According to a BBC spokesperson, "There has been no impact to the transit service, to our safety systems or to our customer's personal information. As the incident is still under investigation, we cannot provide further details at this time." The Municipal Transportation Agency (Muni) is responsible for managing trains, trams, and buses in the city.

The British duo lost to Belgians Moreno de Pauw and Kenny de Ketele in the madison, the final race. Wiggins, 36, who intends to retire following the Ghent Six Day event in November, suggested he might reconsider, quipping, "Money talks." He added, "Who wouldn't want to return after a week like this? I'm unsure. I enjoy racing." The five-time Olympic champion felt that the Lee Valley velodrome, the site of the London 2012 track events and built where he trained as a youth at the Eastway facility, was a fitting location to conclude his British career. Speaking to Eurosport, he said it holds "fantastic memories" and he'll "always come back," likely "next year, but in the stands." Wiggins and Cavendish began the event last Tuesday.

According to the Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) report, cockpit recordings indicated that the aircraft was "responding to the pilot's control inputs." The report also stated that pilot Andy Hill was ejected from the plane during the final stages of the crash on August 22nd. The AAIB has not yet determined if Mr. Hill triggered the ejection sequence. The 51-year-old pilot remains in serious but stable condition in the hospital. The report further details that the Hawker Hunter's canopy detached upon initial impact, leading to the release and subsequent ignition of fuel and fuel vapor. The jet broke into four sections, and both Mr. Hill and his seat were ejected from the cockpit. The report clarifies that the ongoing investigation aims to establish whether the pilot deliberately initiated ejection or if the canopy and seat were released due to impact-related damage to the cockpit. On Saturday, March 26th, approximately 200 elite athletes will compete alongside as many as 25,000 amateur runners in a 13.1-mile race. Starting outside Cardiff Castle, the course will conclude on King Edward VII Avenue, located in the city center. Dave Bedford, former world record holder in the 10,000m, praised the route as "flat" and showcasing both "old Cardiff and now the wonderful new Cardiff." The course highlights landmarks such as the Millennium Stadium, Cardiff City Stadium, Penarth Marina, Cardiff Bay Barrage, Wales Millennium Centre, and Roath Park Lake, culminating in a spectacular finish in the city's core. This 2016 event marks the first time the World Half Marathon Championships have been held in Wales. Cardiff, which has hosted an annual half marathon since 2003, anticipates that the World Half Marathon will further enhance the city's standing in the racing world.

A tract of land spanning from Bo'ness Harbour to the site of the old Kinneil colliery will be transformed into a sanctuary for local flora and fauna. This marks the establishment of the second Local Nature Reserve within the Falkirk Council region. The council intends to leverage this designation to secure financial resources for the area's development. This new status signifies a shift for the site, which was dedicated to heavy industrial activities for nearly two centuries until the central colliery ceased operations in 1983. Certain sections of the area were already acknowledged for their ecological significance, with the mudflats and offshore "island" holding a Special Protection Area designation due to their conservation importance. Councillor Adrian Mahoney, head of leisure, tourism, and community, expressed his enthusiasm for the Kinneil foreshore's new status, noting that the year commemorates the 30th anniversary of the closure of Kinneil Colliery, the last mine in the locality.

Envoy Sigrid Kaag's statement came as Syria seemed to have failed to meet Sunday's deadline for removing its chemical weapons, with the complete destruction of the arsenal slated for June 30. The Russian-US agreement to eliminate Syria's chemical weapons program was established the previous year following a deadly sarin gas attack near Damascus. This multinational mission, tasked with eliminating the weapons, is supervised by the UN Security Council and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW). Despite the UN's June 30 deadline for total destruction, Damascus had pledged to complete the removal of its stockpile by April 27, after previously missing several deadlines. Ms. Kaag, who heads the OPCW-UN mission, emphasized that while the majority of the chemical weapons material has been removed, it has not yet been destroyed, which is factored into the June 30 deadline, underscoring the importance of removing the remaining material from the single remaining site.
